items.title: Wycliffe Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: I played with Wynton for almost, since ’89, eleven, going on twelve years... I was the seventh member to join the septet... I was with Wynton Marsalis. This is a great musical situation.

ctx.x: Yeah. I’ve seen you on numerous programs and you’ve been pretty well recorded so far. Your meeting with Wynton was pretty fortuitous.

It was. I remember the day that I met him was in February of 1987. And someone said Wynton Marsalis is going to come by the school. And all the guys that were really into jazz, and it wasn’t very many but everyone knew who Wynton Marsalis was because I believe at that time he had won Grammys in classical and jazz music. And it was like man, Wynton’s coming to the school. Wynton’s coming. I was like okay, whatever. I mean not that — I had heard about him but I was into listening to Louis Armstrong. I said well…
Is there a difference in your opinion of how young jazz players make their mark in today’s music than twenty-five years ago?
